    // The number of nodes along Y.
    NodeRows(self: SampledVectorGrid2D): Integer
        => self.Values.RowCount;

    // The stored vector at node (i, j), with both indices edge-clamped.
    NodeValue(self: SampledVectorGrid2D, i: Integer, j: Integer): Vector2D
        => self.Values.Row(ClampIndex(j, self.NodeRows))[ClampIndex(i, self.NodeColumns)];

    // The component-wise bilinear blend of the four surrounding node vectors.
    Eval(self: SampledVectorGrid2D, p: Point2D): Vector2D {
        var b = self.Grid.Bounds;
        var x = NodeCoordinate(p.X, b.Min.X, b.Max.X, self.Grid.CellCounts.X);
        var y = NodeCoordinate(p.Y, b.Min.Y, b.Max.Y, self.Grid.CellCounts.Y);
        var i = x.Floor.ToInteger;
        var j = y.Floor.ToInteger;
        var u = x - x.Floor;
        var v = y - y.Floor;
        return self.NodeValue(i, j).Lerp(self.NodeValue(i + 1, j), u)
            .Lerp(self.NodeValue(i, j + 1).Lerp(self.NodeValue(i + 1, j + 1), u), v);
    }

    //==
    // # SampledVectorGrid3D

    // The number of nodes along X.
    NodeColumns(self: SampledVectorGrid3D): Integer
        => self.Grid.CellCounts.X + 1;

    // The number of nodes along Y.
    NodeRows(self: SampledVectorGrid3D): Integer
        => self.Grid.CellCounts.Y + 1;

    // The number of nodes along Z.
    NodeLayers(self: SampledVectorGrid3D): Integer
        => self.Grid.CellCounts.Z + 1;

    // The stored vector at node (i, j, k), with every index edge-clamped.
    NodeValue(self: SampledVectorGrid3D, i: Integer, j: Integer, k: Integer): Vector3D {
        var columns = self.NodeColumns;
        var rows = self.NodeRows;
        var ci = ClampIndex(i, columns);
        var cj = ClampIndex(j, rows);
        var ck = ClampIndex(k, self.NodeLayers);
        return self.Values[(ck * rows + cj) * columns + ci];
    }

    // The component-wise trilinear blend of the eight surrounding node vectors.
    Eval(self: SampledVectorGrid3D, p: Point3D): Vector3D {
        var b = self.Grid.Bounds;
        var x = NodeCoordinate(p.X, b.Min.X, b.Max.X, self.Grid.CellCounts.X);
        var y = NodeCoordinate(p.Y, b.Min.Y, b.Max.Y, self.Grid.CellCounts.Y);
        var z = NodeCoordinate(p.Z, b.Min.Z, b.Max.Z, self.Grid.CellCounts.Z);
        var i = x.Floor.ToInteger;
        var j = y.Floor.ToInteger;
        var k = z.Floor.ToInteger;
        var u = x - x.Floor;
        var v = y - y.Floor;
        var w = z - z.Floor;
        var lo = self.NodeValue(i, j, k).Lerp(self.NodeValue(i + 1, j, k), u)
            .Lerp(self.NodeValue(i, j + 1, k).Lerp(self.NodeValue(i + 1, j + 1, k), u), v);
        var hi = self.NodeValue(i, j, k + 1).Lerp(self.NodeValue(i + 1, j, k + 1), u)
            .Lerp(self.NodeValue(i, j + 1, k + 1).Lerp(self.NodeValue(i + 1, j + 1, k + 1), u), v);
        return lo.Lerp(hi, w);
    }

    //==
    // # SampledColorGrid2D
    //
    // The blend is per channel in whatever space the samples are stored in. That
    // is right for linear-light samples and wrong for gamma-encoded ones; this
    // vocabulary's `Color` is linear light (color.types.plato), so it is right
    // here.

    // The number of nodes along X.
    NodeColumns(self: SampledColorGrid2D): Integer
        => self.Values.ColumnCount;

    // The number of nodes along Y.
    NodeRows(self: SampledColorGrid2D): Integer
        => self.Values.RowCount;

    // The stored color at node (i, j), with both indices edge-clamped.
    NodeValue(self: SampledColorGrid2D, i: Integer, j: Integer): Color
        => self.Values.Row(ClampIndex(j, self.NodeRows))[ClampIndex(i, self.NodeColumns)];

    // The channel-wise bilinear blend of the four surrounding node colors.
    Eval(self: SampledColorGrid2D, p: Point2D): Color {
        var b = self.Grid.Bounds;
        var x = NodeCoordinate(p.X, b.Min.X, b.Max.X, self.Grid.CellCounts.X);
        var y = NodeCoordinate(p.Y, b.Min.Y, b.Max.Y, self.Grid.CellCounts.Y);
        var i = x.Floor.ToInteger;
        var j = y.Floor.ToInteger;
        var u = x - x.Floor;
        var v = y - y.Floor;
        return self.NodeValue(i, j).Lerp(self.NodeValue(i + 1, j), u)
            .Lerp(self.NodeValue(i, j + 1).Lerp(self.NodeValue(i + 1, j + 1), u), v);
    }

    //==
    // # Determinism: what a Seed promises
    //
    // Every seeded generator below draws its randomness from the integer hashing
    // in `noise.library.plato` — `LatticeHash` and `HashToUnit` — and never from a
    // stateful generator. There is no stream to advance and no state to carry, so
    // a Seed names a FUNCTION rather than a position: the dart thrown at cell
    // (i, j) on attempt a depends only on (Seed, i, j, a), and the k-th sample of
    // stratum s only on (Seed, s, k).
    //
    // Three consequences worth stating, because they are what a caller relies on:
    //
    //   * SAME SEED, SAME POINTS. One pattern record always yields the same points,
    //     in the same order, on every backend. The mixing is whole-number
    //     arithmetic that wraps rather than floating point, which is what makes
    //     C#, TypeScript, GLSL and CUDA agree bit for bit.
    //   * ORDER DOES NOT MATTER. Nothing has to be generated in sequence for the
    //     k-th point to be right, so a backend may evaluate the closed-form
    //     patterns in parallel, or evaluate one point of them, and get the same
    //     answer. (The Poisson-disk scan is the one exception, and it is sequential
    //     by construction rather than by its random source: a cell's dart is still
    //     a pure function of the seed, but whether the dart is KEPT depends on the
    //     cells before it.)
    //   * THE CONSTANTS ARE NOT THE CONTRACT. The mixing constants live in
    //     `noise.library.plato` and may change between library versions. A Seed
    //     reproduces a point set within one version of this library, not across
    //     versions; nothing here is a file format.
    //
    // The unseeded families — Halton, Hammersley, Sobol, plastic — carry no Seed at
    // all. The sequence IS the pattern, and the only freedom a caller has is where
    // in it to start.

    // A uniform number in [0, 1) drawn from three whole numbers: the seed, an
    // index identifying WHAT is being drawn for, and a stream index separating
    // several draws for the same thing. All three arguments are the state.
    SampleUnit(seed: Integer, index: Integer, stream: Integer): Number
        => HashToUnit(LatticeHash(seed, index, stream));

    //==
    // # Low-discrepancy sequences
    //
    // Deterministic sequences that fill the unit square more evenly than
    // independent random points do: the discrepancy of the first n terms falls
    // like log(n)^2 / n instead of like 1 / sqrt(n), which is what makes them the
    // default for Monte Carlo integration.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low-discrepancy_sequence
    //
    // They are not blue noise and should not be mistaken for it. Their power
    // spectrum is not isotropic — Halton and Sobol carry strong structure along
    // the axes — so they integrate better than blue noise and LOOK worse. The
    // radial spectrum reading at the end of this file separates the two claims.

    // The fractional part of x, in [0, 1). The wrap every additive recurrence
    // below ends on.
    UnitFraction(x: Number): Number
        => x - x.Floor;
